source.title: Evaluating the Robustness of Analogical Reasoning in Large Language Models

confidence_rationale: Tests the emergent-analogy result directly: on letter-string, digit-matrix and story-analogy variants that probe the same abstract structure but are unlike pre-training data, human performance stays high while GPT models decline sharply on letter-string variants. This weakens the strongest artificial-system evidence that analogy emerges without explicit structure-mapping. Verified only through search-engine records of the arXiv listing (2411.14215) and its TMLR publication; the proxy blocks arXiv and OpenReview, so I read no more than the abstract-level description.
failure_signatures: LLM fragility on counterfactual variants may reflect training distribution rather than the absence of a mapping mechanism; newer or reasoning-tuned models may behave differently, so this is a snapshot.
Weakening LLM emergence does not weaken emergence from a structured relational map; an LLM is not the MECH-419/MECH-420/MECH-300 stack.

mapping.source_claim_statement: GPT models' analogy-making performance declines sharply on letter-string analogy variants that test the same abstract reasoning but are unlikely to resemble pre-training data, while human performance remains high, suggesting reliance on similarity to training data rather than robust abstract reasoning.
mapping.ree_translation: Counterweight to the emergent-analogy evidence under Q-074: surface-independent mapping (the defining property in MECH-421's title, 'regardless of surface features') is exactly what fails when the surface is made unfamiliar. It adds a falsifier requirement for any REE emergence test: transfer must survive surface-novel and counterfactual variants, not only familiar ones.
mapping.mapping_caveat: About LLMs trained on text, not about emergence in a grounded relational map. It weakens the analogy from 'LLMs show analogy emerges' to REE; it does not show a traversal-based substrate would fail.
mapping.source_context: Behavioral comparison of humans and GPT models on original and counterfactual variants of letter-string analogies, digit matrices and story analogies.

confidence_components.notes: TMLR peer-reviewed per search records; metadata verified via search results only, no full-text read.
